Pulmonology · published research

Lung hemorrhage

In rats with immune-complex lung injury, 650-nm laser treatment reduced the hemorrhagic index and myeloperoxidase activity versus untreated controls. Dexamethasone reduced the hemorrhagic index slightly more than laser treatment.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In rats with immune-complex lung injury, 650-nm laser treatment reduced the hemorrhagic index and myeloperoxidase activity versus untreated controls. Dexamethasone reduced the hemorrhagic index slightly more than laser treatment.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Respiratory system > Lung hemorrhage category contains one controlled animal publication and no human trial. It examines experimentally induced immune-complex hemorrhage and short-term tissue markers rather than clinical bleeding or recovery.

Human and clinical evidence

No patient study of PBM for lung hemorrhage was identified in the assigned category.

Animal evidence

Aimbire et al. randomly allocated 49 male Wistar rats with immune-complex lung injury to seven groups, including laser, anti-inflammatory drugs, and control. At 24 hours, 650-nm low-level laser treatment at 2.6 J/cm2 reduced the hemorrhagic index and myeloperoxidase activity compared with untreated controls. Dexamethasone reduced the hemorrhagic index slightly more than laser, while its effect on myeloperoxidase did not differ significantly from laser (2007, DOI 10.1089/pho.2006.1041, PubMed).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell, tissue, or ex-vivo study is listed. The measured lung tissue markers come from the rat experiment.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The investigators used a 650-nm gallium-aluminum-arsenide laser at 2.6 J/cm2 and assessed injury after 24 hours. Wavelength is the light's color band and influences how it interacts with tissue. This single exposure cannot establish an effective or safe clinical regimen.

Interpretation

The experiment shows improvement in two acute injury markers in one animal model, with dexamethasone slightly stronger for the hemorrhagic index. Replication and studies of lung function, survival, and safety are required before the result can guide patient care.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for reduced hemorrhagic injury markers in one controlled rat experiment No direct human evidence identified
Publications and records1 title (exact Respiratory system > Lung hemorrhage)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Only one controlled experiment studied immune-complex lung hemorrhage, and it measured short-term tissue injury in rats. No patient treatment study or independent replication is listed. Replication across injury models and follow-up periods would be needed before evaluating a clinical study.
